newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TURKEY AND BELGIUM BATTLE FOR SECOND PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TURKEY AND BELGIUM BATTLE FOR SECOND PLACE.

text.p: The battle for what will almost certainly be second place in group seven of the European World Cup qualifiers comes to a head in Istanbul on Wednesday.

Turkey, riding high after their defeat of the Netherlands earlier in the month, take on Belgium, who need a win to stamp their authority over the Turks and continue their campaign to reach a place in France next year.
"We've come to Istanbul to get points," Belgium coach George Leekens told reporters on arrival in Turkey.
With group leaders the Netherlands almost certain to extend their lead after their match with lowly San Marino, a win is important for both the Turks and the Belgians..
With only three qualifiers to play after Wednesday's match, defeat for either country -- but especially the Turks, would seriously hamper their chances of qualifying.
The Netherlands top the group with 12 points from five matches, followed by Belgium on nine from four and Tiurkey seven from four.
"Losing or drawing are not in my vocabulary. The only aim is to win," Turkey's coach, Mustafa Denizli told reporters.
Turkey, after their 1-0 defeat of the Netherlands, are confident that they can use their home advantage to overcome Belgium.
"We are actually a much better team than Belgium, but we were unlucky in the game before against them, we were lucky against the Dutch, now the luck is even," Denizli said.
Belgian captain Enzo Scifo is back in Leeken's team after missing the last two games of the campaign due to injury and makes up the only change to the team which beat Wales last month.
Meanwhile, Denizli's squad has been plagued with injuries with key-defender Ilker Yagcioglu, whose cross led to Turkey's goal in the Netherlands match, ruled-out due to a calf-muscle injury.
With other defensive players out through injury or suspension, Denizli has brought in Ali Guncar of Besiktas who is expected to act as sweeper.

Turkey - Rustu Recber (Fenerbahce), Ali Guncar, (Besiktas), Bulent Korkmaz (Galatasaray), Tolunay Kafkas (Trabzonspor), Tayfur Havutcu (Kocaelispor), Oguz Cetin (Istanbulspor), Tayfun Korkut (Fenerbahce), Ogun Temizkanoglu (Trabzonspor), Hakan Sukur (Galatasaray), Tugay Kerimoglu (Galatasaray), Celil Sagir (Samsunspor).

Belgium - Filip De Wilde (Sporting Lisbon), Bertrand Crasson (Napoli), Bart De Roover (Lierse), Eric Van Meir (Lierse), Rudy Smidts (Antwerp), Franky Van der Elst (Club Brugge), Lorenzo Staelens (Club Brugge), Enzo Scifo (Monaco), Nico Van Kerckhoven (Lierse), Luis Oliveira (Fiorentina), Emile Lokonda Mpenza (Mouscron).
